title: Default zero slippage on BalancerPooler enables sandwich attacks on every mint via 3-parameter mint() overload
description: The BalancerPooler sets minBptAmountOut to 0 by default when extraData is empty. The 3-parameter mint() function in NFTMinter (line 116-118) always passes empty extraData to _executeMint, making it structurally impossible for users of this simpler overload to specify slippage protection. Every mint routed through the 3-parameter overload to a BalancerPooler dispatcher is vulnerable to sandwich attacks. An attacker can front-run the addLiquidity call, manipulate pool prices, and extract value from the minter. While the 4-parameter mint() overload exists for passing slippage, the simpler overload is the default entry point and provides no protection.
impact: Value leak on each Balancer-routed mint via sandwich attack. The protocol receives fewer BPT than fair value, permanently diluting the accumulated liquidity position.
rootCause: minBptAmountOut defaults to 0 when extraData is empty (line 66). The 3-parameter mint() overload provides no path for users to specify slippage.
recommendation: Either revert when extraData is empty for BalancerPooler dispatchers, compute a reasonable minimum BPT on-chain based on current pool state, or add an owner-configurable minimum slippage floor.
